conclusion: Mixed: Runner rated higher; Corp remained in the same range; Vantage was unchanged. No broad rating uplift established.

method.reviewers: Three fresh-context AI critics; earlier scores withheld and prior/current sibling reports forbidden before rating. Initial inherited-context attempts were cancelled before any gameplay or rating and excluded.
method.sample: One natural game per perspective, new seeds. Gateway deck matchups repeated; Vantage now uses recommended Vic/Editorial lists rather than the earlier Vic/Weyland interaction pilots.
method.limits: Subjective holistic scores from AI reviewers, not a human usability study or statistically established improvement. Differences include gameplay strategy and outcomes; cannot isolate UI changes.

positives: Working identity/card readers and deck setup guidance.
Clearer cost and encounter explanations; useful wrong-type and virus guidance.
Coherent visual organization and no observed application crashes in these games.

remainingPriorities.evidence: Corp reviewer faced one early Runner run, then repeated unchallenged scoring. Vantage reviewer felt routine central pressure against a Corp without a scoring clock.
remainingPriorities.caveat: These seeds do not establish a universal AI defect. A postgame offline audit found Vantage Corp agendas in hand only at early recorded decisions, so lack of later scoring is not proof it ignored legal scoring opportunities.
